Findings.Title: The alias API is still designed only in the derived plan
Findings.Defect: C2 defers its interface to TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008 AC-007. Only the plan defines four public PowerShell alias functions and the consumer-delivery data model. The architecture has no shared alias-access component in section 3.5.6 with those contracts and its test seam.
Evidence: Architecture line 251 says the interface is locked in TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008 AC-007. The architecture contains no Register-McpAliasConsumer, Get-McpUnacknowledgedAlias, Get-McpAlias, or Confirm-McpAliasAcknowledged definition.

Plan line 811 defines all four signatures, null/ambiguous lookup outcomes, permanent lookup entries, prunable delivery entries, and the consumer set captured at alias commit. Live writes and replay both consume the alias journal, so this is shared behavior, not merely a catalog label.
Findings.SpecificChange: Move the complete alias model and four function contracts, error/return behavior, immutable host binding, atomicity and replay rules into one section 3.5.6 component owned by PluginCorePowerShell with one named Pester test seam. Make every alias caller reference it and derive AC-007 from it. No public contract may remain defined only in the plan.
Findings.Regression: Architecture restructuring left an explicit design dependency on the plan.

Findings.Title: A trusted response can depend on a response that is no longer trusted
Findings.Defect: IResponseStalenessRule compares dependency hashes but never evaluates the effective trust/status of a PriorResponse dependency. PriorResponse and Package hashes are immutable content hashes. Dependency rejection, supersession, demotion, or staleness therefore does not invalidate descendants.
Evidence: Counterexample: trusted B is included in the package that produces trusted A. Reject B, or change a file that B depends on. B becomes Rejected or effectively Stale, but its ContentSha256 and the package ContentSha256 do not change. Every hash tested for A still matches; lines 464-465 return Fresh and A remains eligible for trusted retrieval.

The rule explicitly special-cases deleted/superseded requirements, but has no corresponding prior-response status or recursive dependency check. Read-time freshness added for R4-F5 fixes direct changed-file reads but not this chain.
Findings.SpecificChange: Extend the one shared staleness rule to validate effective trust and freshness of PriorResponse dependencies, including dependencies reached through packages. Define cycle handling and per-read memoization. Cover B becoming stale, rejected, superseded, or demoted while A content is unchanged; queries must exclude A immediately and EvaluateStaleness must persist the dependent invalidation.
Findings.Regression: The R4 direct-read fix is present; its shared rule still admits an invalid trusted dependency chain.

Findings.Title: Package recovery and supersession discard part of the turn key
Findings.Defect: The architecture declares the turn identity to be Agent + SessionId + RequestId, but recovery queries only requestId, invocation idempotency uses only requestId, and the supersede guard compares only requestId. Legacy turns with the same requestId in different sessions remain legal.
Evidence: The live database has a unique session key (WorkspaceId, SourceType, SessionId) and a unique turn key (SessionLogId, RequestId). The new workspace-wide minted-id index explicitly excludes legacy rows (Addendum A.2).

Two legal turns with the same requestId can have distinct Built packages through the public build API. The fallback at line 3806 selects the newest package by requestId without the bound session/agent. Supersede at line 3486 likewise accepts a replacement belonging to the other turn. A workspace-wide idempotency key of requestId also collides for such roots.
Findings.SpecificChange: Carry and check the full immutable turn key at recovery, submission binding, and supersession. Add an agent filter to package queries, require all three root fields when recovering the bound package, and derive a bounded deterministic invocation idempotency key from the full root. Test same requestId in two legacy sessions and two agents, including wrong-package recovery and cross-turn supersession refusal.
Findings.Regression: The new root-id reconciliation is correct in the entities but incomplete at operational uses.

Findings.Title: The PowerShell port removes working tool-audit behavior
Findings.Defect: The host-limit row drops beforeTool/afterTool and tool.execute.before/after solely because the PowerShell core has no audit hook. That is an unimplemented port, not a host infrastructure limitation. It contradicts C6 and removes behavior the approved Phase A contract preserved.
Evidence: At cline-v2 e776d942, lines 250-275 call core.appendToolAction before and after a tool. At opencode 36ed34d9, lines 226-254 do the same. The approved live TODO description and current architecture C6 require tool runs as tool_call/tool_result dialog items; QB-AGENT-001 owns the later tool_execution taxonomy, not permission to discard these existing records.
The adapter allowlist excludes these hooks. The architecture lists the removal as a limitation but supplies neither an operator decision allowing it nor a replacement audit path and its parity tests.
Findings.SpecificChange: Port the shared existing tool-audit behavior into the PowerShell core, define its hook input/output and error contract once, forward all four native hooks through the logic-free adapters, and preserve the tool_call/tool_result records under the bound turn identity. Carry the affected host/core tests and requirement reconciliation in that same change before retiring the Node path.
Findings.Regression: PowerShell convergence currently deletes supported behavior; the operator authorized a port, not this deletion.

Findings.Title: The replace sequence permits a completion-gate bypass
Findings.Defect: CompletionGate correctly applies to every Replace carrying completed or failed, including an already-terminal turn. The common sequence rule and Replace sequence narrow it to a status transition and recommend replacing without moving to a terminal status.
Evidence: A PUT of an already completed turn that omits its reviews is a replacement, not an additive enrichment. Lines 2314 and 2323 require re-gating it. Lines 1466 and 1732 do not, so following that sequence resets required review evidence while preserving completed.
This is a conflicting executable branch, not a wording preference: the two definitions yield different responses to the same request.
Findings.SpecificChange: Use the exact CompletionGate predicate in the common sequence rule and Replace sequence: a transition into completed/failed OR a Replace carrying either status. Show an already-completed replacement missing reviews returning the gate refusal. Keep additive terminal enrichment exempt. Add the corresponding negative case to the owning TEST statement.
Findings.Regression: A holistic Phase B diagram inconsistency remains after the round-4 surface corrections.

Findings.Title: First-ingress and mint-recovery instructions still contradict each other
Findings.Defect: The nested mint activity says every answered mint clears the write-ahead record, while the authoritative retry rule retains final refusals with drainAttempts=1. The open-session sequence records mcpSessionId only after confirmed open, while first-ingress and SessionStart persist it before calling open so an outage cannot change the binding.
Evidence: For a final validation_error answer, line 991 keeps the record for bounded replay/quarantine; line 1015 clears it. This is the same final-refusal recovery defect R4-F8 required removing.

For the first open timing out, lines 992/1026 retain the chosen MCP session identity, but line 1873 does not record it. Retrying under a newly generated identity can split the host session and strand its bound records.
Findings.SpecificChange: Make all activities, lead-ins, and sequences use the shared classification and one lifecycle rule: success/merged-terminal/equal-field fail-close clear as specified; outage retains; final refusal retains and counts the first attempt. Persist the selected MCP session identity before the first open and reuse it after every outage. Add exact first-ingress outage and final-refusal readback cases.
Findings.Regression: R4-F8 and its inherited R3-F6 remain NOT RESOLVED despite correct branches elsewhere.

Findings.Title: Overlapping projection passes can orphan GraphRAG documents
Findings.Defect: The deduplication rule preserves an overlapping document only when the row is Projected. A rejection during two concurrent ingests makes both saves Pending and lets the second overwrite the only stored document id. A post-ingest save exhaustion or failed duplicate cleanup also has no durable cleanup record.
Evidence: Concrete interleaving: passes P1/P2 both read Trusted with no projection and ingest D1/D2; Reject commits; P1 stores Pending+D1; P2 sees Pending, not Projected, and stores Pending+D2. The next pass deletes D2 and loses every reference to D1.

The cited live IngestTextAsync allocates adhoc-<new Guid> on every call. The single GraphRagDocumentId column cannot retain both pending cleanup obligations. The four-attempt 409 path after external ingest similarly exits without defining how the new document is recovered.
Findings.SpecificChange: Define durable per-response projection ownership or an outbox/operation record before ingest, with idempotent completion and a durable set of documents awaiting deletion. Preserve cleanup obligations in every row state and after failed saves/deletes. Test two ingests plus rejection, save exhaustion after ingest, and duplicate-delete failure; later passes must remove every untrusted/orphan document.
Findings.Regression: The overlapping-Projected fix handles the happy interleaving but loses the reject/cleanup interleavings.

Findings.Title: The model-grade acceptance checks do not fully establish the claimed evidence
Findings.Defect: runtime_identity requires every turn_context to match but requires no turn_context to exist. A rollout containing only the matching session_meta passes that predicate without proving model or effort. Separately, verdict_match compares scores/findings but defines no verdict consistency rule for its required DISAGREE-with-passing-scores negative case.
Evidence: An empty set satisfies the universal test at line 2811. Matching request_meta, thread.started and session_meta identifiers are declarations/bindings, not the required live model/effort evidence.

Line 2813 requires ModelGradeDisagreeVerdictPassingScoresRefusedVerdictMatch, but neither check 5 nor the per-response grades schema at line 3718 contains the predicate or per-entry verdict semantics needed to produce that refusal. This is especially ambiguous for a range with mixed passing and failing responses.
Findings.SpecificChange: Require at least one review-run turn_context and bind its model/effort and thread to the completed review being graded; refuse missing runtime context explicitly. Define per-response verdict semantics and the batch overall verdict, validate their consistency with scores/findings, and make the named negative test match that rule without preventing legitimate failing grades or mixed ranges from being recorded.
Findings.Regression: Live identity comparison is present, but missing evidence can still pass; the required verdict negative case has no defined acceptance rule.

Findings.Title: Single-turn transaction scope still includes a shared session write
Findings.Defect: The locked turn-level decision isolates the turn and moves the session summary to a separate post-commit write. The shared SerializableWrite definition and Phase B write contract still read and write the common session row inside every single-turn transaction while promising different turns never conflict.
Evidence: Two different turns in one session address the same session row under the stated Serializable delegate. Concurrent updates to that shared row require serialization and can consume the same bounded transient-conflict retries the architecture exposes as 409.

Line 152 explicitly makes summary refresh a separate write whose failure cannot fail the turn. Lines 332 and 2125 do not identify any other permitted session-row mutation or reconcile their in-transaction write with that decision.
Findings.SpecificChange: Make the one shared transaction contract match the locked decision: locate/validate the parent as needed, but mutate only the target turn and its children inside a single-turn transaction; specify the session summary update as a separate post-commit operation with its own non-failing outcome. Define the provider-specific locking/read strategy and test concurrent writes to different turns plus a failed summary refresh.
Findings.Regression: The round-5 turn-level reconciliation was not propagated consistently into the shared component and review units.
